title: fix(app-shell): the environment permission door degrades the display, not the save, when the post-save re-read rejects
body:
Fixes #9484

## What moved

At environment scope (no `packageId`) `doSave` in `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` re-anchors its
display baseline by awaiting `client.layered` **after** `client.save` has already returned. That
read carried no rejection handler, so a transport failure on it fell into the same `catch` that
renders a failed save. One re-read failure, three wrong outcomes, for a permission write that had
**landed**:

1. the red error strip rendered the transport's message;
2. `resetDraftBaseline` was skipped, so `isDirty` stayed true — the editor kept claiming unsaved
   changes and the browser's "leave site?" guard kept firing on a record that was already
   persisted;
3. `setDestructive(null)` was skipped, so a forced save left its destructive-change dialog open
   over a change that had already been committed.

A rejection there now degrades the **display only**. The save reads as the success it was; the
baseline is re-anchored from the body the server just accepted (the fallback that line already
spelled for the resolved-but-empty envelope); the dialog closes; and the author is still told the
re-read failed — on a separate advisory notice (amber, `role="status"`, new designer-table key
`perm.save.rereadStale`) that opens with "Saved." and then says the matrix on screen is the saved
body rather than a fresh read from the server.

**Nothing about what is written changes.** The environment door still PUTs the whole record with
the same options, and the pre-existing guard test in the same file keeps pinning exactly that.

## The fence was held

The package door's **pre-save** re-read is untouched, and the two are deliberately not unified:
there the read happens *before* the write and its rejection refuses the write on purpose (raised
as objectui#9420), because merging a package slice onto a stale base deletes every other
package's permission rows. Turning that into a degraded display would be a far worse defect than
the one repaired here.

The whole diff to the editor **removes exactly three lines**, and none of them belongs to either
control:

```
$ git diff origin/main..HEAD -- packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx | grep -E '^-[^-]'
-    setDraft(next);
-        const lay = await client.layered TYPEARG (type, payload.name);
-        resetDraftBaseline(toDisplayDraft((lay.effective ?? toSave) as PermissionSetDraft));
```

(The removed line's generic type argument is written as the word TYPEARG above: GitHub's body
sanitizer deletes tag-shaped fragments even inside fenced code, and a line quoted to show what was
removed cannot afford to arrive with a hole in it.)

The load-path `client.layered(...).catch(() => null)` and the package door's `rereadFailed`
`.catch` are byte-identical to `main`.

## A second mechanism, measured, that the card does not name

Making the re-read's rejection non-fatal is **not** enough to close consequence 2. `isDirty` is a
`useMemo` keyed on `draft`, while the anchor it compares against lives in a ref. On this arm the
re-anchor falls back to the saved body, which at environment scope *is* the current `draft`
object — so `setDraft` bailed out on `Object.is`, the memo never recomputed, and the editor went
on reporting dirty against an anchor that already said clean.

This was measured, not reasoned: the first version of this fix called `resetDraftBaseline` and
the unload-guard assertion still failed. `resetDraftBaseline` now always hands `setDraft` a fresh
shallow copy (the anchor is a JSON snapshot, so a copy is anchor-identical). Leg 2 of the reverse
verification below is that one line's own ablation.

## Pins — the existing harness, extended

No second harness: the four new cases live in
`PermissionMatrixEditor.packageDoorRereadRefusal.test.tsx`, which already drives a client whose
`layered` answers the published record for the load and rejects from the second call on. Each
consequence is asserted through what the component exposes, never through an internal:

- **consequence 1** — the transport's message is absent from the page while the advisory notice is
  present and carries `role="status"`, and the package door's refusal wording stays off this door;
- **consequence 2** — `onDirtyChange` (the prop the Studio Access pillar's unsaved-changes guard
  hangs on) reports `false`, and a real `beforeunload` event dispatched at the window comes back
  with `defaultPrevented === false`. Both are read after a control in the same test proves the
  edit had armed the guard, so "disarmed" is a transition and not a listener that was never
  installed;
- **consequence 3** — reached the only way it is observable: let the server raise the 409 that
  opens the destructive-change dialog, force the save, let the post-save re-read reject, and
  assert the dialog is gone.

Each pin has a resolving-arm control in the same harness, so the absences are readable.

## Reverse verification

Both legs ran from the committed fix. Each mutation was proven to have reached disk (blob hash
compared against the `HEAD` blob, plus a before/after count of the text being removed) before its
run, and the restore leg was proven byte-identical to `HEAD` with an empty `git diff HEAD`
afterwards.

| leg | mutation | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the whole editor file reverted to `origin/main` (on-disk blob `88c94dad` vs `HEAD` blob `7048a337`) | **2 failed / 6 passed.** `queryByText('layered read failed')` found a span (consequence 1); `queryByText('Destructive change')` found the dialog heading (consequence 3). Both resolving-arm controls stayed green. |
| 2 | only `setDraft({ ...next })` reverted to `setDraft(next)`, the rejection handler left in place (removed-text count 1 to 0, injected-text count 1, on-disk blob `92508ec0`) | **1 failed / 7 passed.** `expect(onDirtyChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(false)` failed (consequence 2). |
| restore | `git checkout HEAD -- path` | on-disk blob back to `7048a337`, `git diff HEAD` empty. |

Leg 1 stops at the first consequence and never reaches the dirty assertion, which is why leg 2
exists: together they give each of the three consequences its own pre-fix red, and leg 2 does it
under a strictly weaker mutation.

## Verification

All at the final commit, `git rev-parse --short HEAD` = `56cade5e5`.

| check | command | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the pin file | `pnpm exec vitest run ...packageDoorRereadRefusal.test.tsx` | 8 passed (8) |
| the whole editor family | `pnpm exec vitest run ...metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor` | 15 files, 73 passed |
| the whole affected directory | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` (under the shared serialisation lock; VERDICT command-exit 0, held 5m26s) | **267 files, 2835 passed, 1 skipped** |
| downstream renderers of the page | `PackageOwdOverviewPanel`, `StudioDesignSurface.pillarNavGuard`, `studio-locale.i18n` | 3 files, 22 passed |
| dependency closure build | `turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/app-shell^..." --concurrency=2` (under the lock) | 28 of 28 successful |
| typecheck | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) | exit 0 |
| lint | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run lint` — the affected package's own script, which is what CI runs | exit 0, **0 errors**, 3031 warnings, all pre-existing |
| gates | `check:control-bytes`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape` | all exit 0 |
| governed surface | `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the four changed paths | NOT GOVERNED — 0 of 5 surfaces matched |

Exit codes were captured before any pipe (`cmd redirected-to-file; EXIT=$?`), never read through
`| tail`.

Lint scope, stated so the reading is checkable rather than asserted: the population is the one
eslint's own flat config selects for `packages/app-shell` — **1172 files**, counted off the length
of its `--format json` output, not estimated. `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions`,
`project` or `projectService`, so type-aware linting is not enabled and this diff cannot move the
verdict of any file it does not itself contain. A harsher `--no-inline-config` run over the same
1172 files reports 16 errors; all 16 are in files this branch does not touch and all are inline
`eslint-disable` sites that the CI invocation honours. The three changed files report 0 errors
under both invocations, and every one of their 25 warnings sits on a line this diff did not add.

Not measured locally, by design: the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` farms, and the rest of
`packages/app-shell` outside `views/metadata-admin/` (711 test files in the package; 267 of them
ran here). CI owns those.

## Clause-2, re-measured at delivery

`no`. The component is absent from the package entry: `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` names its
metadata-admin leaves individually and `PermissionMatrixEditor` / `PermissionMatrixEditPage` is
not among them (control — 84 `^export` lines in that entry, matching the dispatch's own reading;
11 of them are named metadata-admin leaf re-exports). Counted off the diff actually pushed rather
than reported as a floor: `git diff BASE..HEAD | grep -cE '^\+export'` is **0**, and the diff adds
no export anywhere — the new state, the new handler and the new notice are all inside a component
body, and the new i18n key is a row in a module-local table.

## Acceptance notes

Observed while working, deliberately **not** repaired here and not carded (neither a reproducible
defect, nor a declared-contract breach, nor an authoring-metadata trap):

- The load path's `stripReadDecorations` docblock still explains itself by saying that `doSave`'s
  fresh read has a `.catch(() => null)` arm which "falls back to this very body and spreads it
  into `client.save`". That arm became a refusal in objectui#9420, so the sentence's mechanism is
  historical; this branch adds a `.catch(() => null)` on the *other* door whose fallback never
  reaches `client.save` at all, which makes the paragraph read as if it describes this change when
  it does not. Doc drift only — the `stripReadDecorations` call it justifies is still correct and
  still needed. Whoever next edits the load path or `stripReadDecorations` is the one who will
  read it.
